what.text: Sertraline is an antidepressant of the SSRI type (selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor). It blocks nerve cells from taking back serotonin, a chemical messenger, so more of it stays active in the brain and spinal cord. It has only very weak effects on two other messengers, noradrenaline and dopamine.

The brand Zoloft comes as tablets and an oral solution. Delayed or absent ejaculation is a known side effect of SSRIs, and that side effect is why sertraline has been studied for premature ejaculation.
Adonis lists sertraline, from the Beluga catalog, as a compounded prescription product. Its form is not on file, so it is not described here.
Sertraline is FDA approved for depression and five other psychiatric uses. It is not approved for premature ejaculation; that use is off-label. A compounded sertraline product is not FDA approved.

research.text: For premature ejaculation (PE), the evidence is small randomized trials, with 36 to 147 men each, mostly 4 to 8 weeks long, plus a 2019 pooled analysis. They mainly measured time to ejaculation. No regulator we checked has approved sertraline for PE.
Each study is listed below as it was run. All are off-label uses.

research.title: Sertraline for PE, 1995 (USA)

facts.v: randomized, placebo-controlled, after a 1-week placebo run-in
52 heterosexual men with self-reported PE
8 weeks
self-reported time to ejaculation, successful attempts at intercourse, ejaculation during foreplay

research.found: Time to ejaculation and successful attempts improved more on sertraline than placebo. The authors said most men tolerated it well.

src.label: Mendels J, et al. J Clin Psychopharmacol 1995;15(5):341-6

research.title: Fluoxetine, sertraline and clomipramine for PE, 1998 (Korea)

facts.v: double-blind, placebo-controlled; each man took each drug and placebo in turn
36 men (mean age 44) with ejaculation within 2 minutes of penetration
4 weeks per drug
self-reported time to ejaculation, satisfaction, side effects

research.found: Average time to ejaculation rose from 46 seconds to 2.27 minutes on placebo, 2.30 on fluoxetine, 4.27 on sertraline and 5.75 on clomipramine. Clomipramine had more side effects than the others.

src.label: Kim SC, Seo KK. J Urol 1998;159(2):425-7

research.title: Sertraline for PE, 1998 (Australia)

facts.v: randomized, single-blind, placebo-controlled crossover, then open-label treatment
37 men aged 19 to 70 in stable relationships
4 weeks per arm; open-label phase averaged 7.3 months
time to ejaculation

research.found: Average time to ejaculation was 3.2 minutes on sertraline and 0.5 minutes on placebo, from 0.3 minutes before. Two men could not ejaculate at all. Of 29 men in the open-label phase, 20 later stopped the drug.

research.title: Sertraline for PE, 1998 (Turkey)

facts.v: randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled
37 men with PE: 22 on sertraline, 15 on placebo
4 weeks
time to ejaculation, side effects

research.found: Time to ejaculation was significantly longer on sertraline. No one stopped because of side effects.

src.label: Biri H, et al. Int Urol Nephrol 1998;30(5):611-5

research.title: Sertraline for PE with a validated questionnaire, 2006

facts.v: randomized, single-blind, placebo-controlled crossover
147 men with PE (77 and 70 in the two groups)
4 weeks on each; follow-up 6 months after stopping
Arabic Index of Premature Ejaculation score

research.found: The summary reports that 127 (81%) of 157 men improved on sertraline; it does not explain why that is more than the 147 enrolled. Of 100 men followed up, 66 had PE return within 6 months of stopping.

src.label: Arafa M, Shamloul R. Int J Impot Res 2006;18(6):534-8

research.title: Pooled analysis of sertraline trials for PE, 2019

facts.v: systematic review and meta-analysis of 12 randomized trials and 2 randomized crossover trials
977 men with PE in total
time to ejaculation, satisfaction of men and partners, side effects

research.found: Sertraline lengthened time to ejaculation and raised satisfaction scores. It raised the risk of stomach upset (risk ratio 2.71).

research.text: FDA approved Zoloft on the basis of placebo-controlled trials in major depression, obsessive-compulsive disorder, panic disorder, PTSD, social anxiety disorder and premenstrual dysphoric disorder.

us.text: Sertraline is FDA approved as Zoloft (first approved 1991) and as generics, for six psychiatric conditions. Premature ejaculation is not an approved use; prescribing it for PE is off-label. As of October 31, 2026.

items.text: Zoloft tablets, NDA 019839. Drugs@FDA data show the original approval on December 30, 1991. The label lists initial U.S. approval as 1991.
major depressive disorder, obsessive-compulsive disorder, panic disorder, post-traumatic stress disorder, social anxiety disorder and premenstrual dysphoric disorder.

antidepressants increased the risk of suicidal thoughts and behavior in children, teenagers and young adults in short-term studies. All patients should be watched closely for worsening and for suicidal thoughts.
no. The label says sertraline is not a controlled substance.

under section 503A, pharmacies may use a bulk substance that has a USP monograph, or is a component of an FDA-approved drug, or is on FDA's 503A list. Sertraline is the active ingredient of approved Zoloft. A compounded sertraline product is still not FDA approved.

src.label: FDA, bulk drug substances under section 503A

us.text: Compounded drugs are not FDA-approved. FDA does not review their safety, effectiveness or quality before they are sold.

world.lead: Sertraline is an approved prescription antidepressant in the US, the UK, the EU (by national approval) and Australia. No regulator we checked lists premature ejaculation as an approved use.

countries.status: Approved medicine (Zoloft, 1991; depression and five other psychiatric uses). Prescription-only. PE use is off-label.

after.text: Sertraline is not named on the WADA 2026 Prohibited List or on the 2027 List, which takes effect January 1, 2027.

side.text: Sertraline's label carries a boxed warning on suicidal thoughts in young people and a warning on sexual side effects. In men, sexual side effects include delayed or failed ejaculation, lower libido and erectile dysfunction, the same effect the PE studies relied on.

items.text: in pooled trials of about 77,000 adults and over 4,400 children and teenagers, suicidal thoughts and behaviors were more common on antidepressants than placebo under age 25: 14 more per 1,000 patients under 18 and 5 more per 1,000 aged 18 to 24. They were less common at 25 and older.
in placebo-controlled trials, ejaculation failure 8% vs 1% on placebo, lower libido 7% vs 2%, erectile dysfunction 4% vs 1%, ejaculation disorder 3% vs 0%, and other male sexual dysfunction 2% vs 0%.

in October 2026 the UK's MHRA said some antidepressants, sertraline among them, are linked to sexual problems that may continue after the medicine is stopped (“PSSD”), and is adding this to UK leaflets.
nausea, diarrhea, tremor, indigestion, lower appetite, sweating, ejaculation failure and lower libido.

serotonin syndrome (higher risk with other serotonin drugs), bleeding risk (higher with aspirin, NSAIDs or blood thinners), triggering mania, seizures, angle-closure glaucoma, low blood sodium, and QT prolongation of the heart rhythm.
stopping suddenly can cause nausea, sweating, dizziness, electric-shock sensations, anxiety, irritability and other symptoms. The label advises a gradual reduction.
pooled data showed a higher risk of stomach upset on sertraline.

surprises: Sertraline is often described as a PE treatment, but no regulator we checked approves it for PE; EMA's 2009 harmonised EU uses do not include it.

The UK's MHRA (October 2026) warns that sexual problems may continue after stopping sertraline; the current US Zoloft label (revised August 2023) describes sexual side effects but does not say they may persist after stopping.
